issue: A stray blank line at `plugins/autopilot/CHANGELOG.md:9` splits the `### Added` list into two loose lists.

resource_closure leaves out many runtime script dependencies. `resource_edges` has 202 rows, yet packaged skills call scripts that are neither packaged nor declared external: `consolidate_findings.py` (plugins/autopilot/skills/run-autopilot/references/lane-solo.md:168, plugins/autopilot/skills/review-work-completion/SKILL.md:386), `compute_mech_facts.py` (plugins/autopilot/skills/fast-track/SKILL.md:270), and also `render_prompt.py`/`record_dispatch.py` in fast-track, `detect_tautological_tests.py`, `check_review_file.py`, `await_reviewer_outputs.py`, `fast_track_plan.py`, `card.py`, `fablectl.py` and `parse_review.py`. The test locks the edge count and digest (tests/autopilot/test_package.py:331), so it cannot catch the gap. The unconditional skill gates block runtime harm today, but later PRDs that restore entry points will inherit this incomplete map

`plugins/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py:41` re-walks the parsed policy by hand (lines 41-49) to find floats. Passing `parse_float` and `parse_constant` hooks that raise `ValueError` to the `json.loads` call at line 36 rejects fractions, exponents and NaN/Infinity while parsing. The behavior is the same, the 9-line loop goes away, and the existing `except ValueError` already turns the error into exit 1.

All 27 behavior rows assigned to 00012 (P03–P05, R01, OPT-042, BEH-001..010, UTIL-*) still show evidence status "planned" with null artifact, sha and revision, and their acceptance cases are "planned". Nothing in the map links this PRD's own obligations to the contracts and tests it delivered, while asset rows carry "passed" receipts

No test checks the policy's rule IDs against the packaged rubric files. The design says to "parse the rule ids from the packaged … rubric.md … and require them to equal rule_ids" and to require that `eve.md` has the de-slop section. Instead, the R, B and D lists are hardcoded constants (`test_contract.py:28-30`), so a wrong list would still pass. The committed data is correct today: it matches R1-R4, R6-R13, B1-B19 and D1-D5 in the packaged files.

`tests/autopilot/test_package.py:203` checks six CHANGELOG bullets word for word, so rewording the changelog breaks a test. The CHANGELOG bytes are already pinned by `destination_blob_sha256` in `test_content_roster` (`tests/autopilot/test_package.py:281`), so this check repeats one that exists and only adds a dependency on the wording. A check for the `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` structure would be enough.
`tools/autopilot/check-source.py:244` has three blank lines between `_audit_behaviors` and `_audit_regressions`. PEP 8 uses two (pycodestyle E303).

`tests/autopilot/test_package.py:69` builds its target from `git archive HEAD`. A local run with uncommitted edits therefore tests the last commit, not the working tree, and can pass on stale bytes. The design asks for this ("committed target inputs"), but neither the module docstring nor the README's Development section says so.

Four named acceptance scenarios have no test of that name: source_inventory_mapping, review_schema, reference_tree_preserved and package_self_contained. Tests under other names cover them (tests/autopilot/test_provenance.py:49, tests/autopilot/test_contract_semantics.py:299, tests/autopilot/test_package.py:286, tests/autopilot/test_package.py:371). The exit criterion "the named task tests pass" can only be checked by hand-mapping

The oracle rejects a review when an activated conditional reviewer (Carl) fails its last attempt (`required_job_failed`). The pinned retry policy says to mark the reviewer unavailable and continue (plugins/autopilot/skills/review-work-completion/references/retry-policy.md:9), and the policy encodes `reviewer_failed_after_retry → mark_unavailable`. Rejecting is right for mandatory jobs but stricter than the source for optional Carl, and no golden case covers that path

The README and CHANGELOG "passed" delivery receipts point at themselves: the artifact is the file itself, and the test checks `tested_package_revision` only with a regex. The receipt proves nothing beyond the file's hash

prerequisites.py counts only regular `NNNNN-<slug>.md` files, but the backlog `eligibility:` lines use `ls done/NNNNN-*`. The "maintainer view of the same table" can disagree with selection, for example on `00012-x.md.bak`

`doubt_label_map` ships in the portable policy, but it comes from the author's personal global AGENTS.md, not the pinned source, and has no source binding. It is author-home content inside a package meant to work without the author

`check-source.py` never reads `review-policy-v1.json`. The design says it recomputes the binding and anchor digests from the pinned blobs. Coverage holds only through two checks that must both run: normal tests compare policy to inventory, and the audit compares inventory to blobs.

`test_rejected_cases_have_exactly_the_specified_complete_semantic_defects` repeats `test_contract_semantics.py:299` for the rejected cases, and `test_package.py:406` runs the same oracle a third time. Lines 63-94 also re-check properties that the `validate_review == accepted` assert at line 42 already enforces.

`ci_autopilot_wired` asserts the exact list of steps in the unrelated `plugins` job. The design says not to snapshot unrelated workflow content, and any future specflow CI step will fail the autopilot suite. An ordered-subsequence check would still prove the job is preserved.

The draft 2020-12 `"type":"integer"` accepts `1.0`, so `attempt: 1.0` passes the schema. The oracle's `range(1, highest + 1)` would then likely raise TypeError instead of returning a defect. The wire test covers 1.5 but not 1.0.

Cannot statically verify: the autopilot suite, `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts` and `python3 scripts/validate.py` pass. The test gate reports exit 0 with no counts, and the fail-first replay was skipped because `requirements-test.txt` does not exist at base.

The gated SKILL.md bodies keep `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and Claude-specific prose. This is known and out of scope: the content is preserved byte for byte behind the first-body refusal gate for AP 00015 to adapt.
The only semantic validator is the test oracle; there is no runtime one. This is by design: task 14 forbids a validator runtime, and AP 00020 owns it.
